name: Runner Extras - Published Application System Table
brief: Issue #2963, corrected by #3066: Published Application (2000000206) is the platform's record of which apps are published. The runner has no publish step, so it seeds one row per loaded app from the manifests it already parses, stamps the same per-app package id onto that app's AllObj rows, and seeds the matching Installed Application (2000000212) row the Installed FlowField is computed over. This suite pins the runner's side of that: the rows, the stamp, and the property that makes the pair mean anything - the package ids discriminate BETWEEN apps.
description: What Published Application CONTAINS is plain BC behaviour and now lives upstream, in the corpus's Target = OnPrem app (BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#187, tests/al-language-onprem/record/TestPublishedApplicationSysTable.al), where a service tier adjudicates it on eight OnPrem legs. It could not go into the Cloud-target corpus app: compiling `Record "Published Application"` there reports `error AL0296: The application object or method 'Published Application' has scope 'OnPrem' and cannot be used for 'Cloud' development`, which is why the corpus grew a second, OnPrem-target app. This suite targets OnPrem for the same reason. What stays HERE is only what the RUNNER does, for a bundle that is not the corpus app: that rows exist at all with nothing published, that this bundle's own manifest is among them, that the blank Tenant ID the runner chose satisfies BC's own '%1|%2' filter, that no two seeded rows collide, and that Installed reads true because the runner seeded 2000000212 rather than by writing to the FlowField. Two claims this suite used to make were runner-local pins of BC behaviour and were both WRONG - that a row's two package columns differ (a real tier reports them equal), and that Installed reads false (a real tier reports true). #3066 removed them, changed the runner to match, and left the corrected claims upstream. The discrimination that remains is BETWEEN apps, and it is the whole point: seeding both sides of `Reten. Pol. Allowed Tbl. Impl.ModuleOwnsTable`'s comparison with the type default would make every app own every table, and every ownership check would pass - for the wrong reason, indistinguishably from a fix.
